newsitem.title: USA: MECHANIC CLEARED IN TENNIS STAR'S DEATH.
newsitem.headline: MECHANIC CLEARED IN TENNIS STAR'S DEATH.

text.p: A swimming pool mechanic and a pool maintenance company were cleared on Friday of criminal charges in the gas poisoning death of former tennis star Vitas Gerulaitis.

A Suffolk County, New York, jury found Bartholomew Torpey and his employer, East End Pools and Courts Inc., not guilty of all charges. They were accused of improperly installing an exhaust pipe in a pool cottage where Gerulaitis died in 1994, aged 40.

Prosecutors argued that Torpey, who was cleared of criminally negligent homicide, rigged an incorrect length of pipe from a pool heating system, trapping carbon monoxide gas near the room in the Southampton, Long Island cottage where Gerulaitis was resting.
The jury, which took three days to reach a verdict, found the pool company not guilty of second-degree manslaughter.

Gerulaitis, who retired from the tennis circuit in 1984 but later returned as a broadcaster and played in exhibition matches, won 27 singles and nine doubles championships, including the 1977 Australian Open.

His mother, Aldona Gerulaitis, has filed a $63 million civil lawsuit in New York City, citing nine defendants, including Torpey, the pool company and Martin Raynes, the friend who owned the estate where Gerulaitis died.
